title: Selection of Model in Developing Information Security Criteria for Smart Grid Security System
review_status: full-text audit complete; requirements/model-selection contribution only; hosted proceedings full text checked; no security-effect experiment
venue_year_verified: arXiv submitted 2011-09-13; record cites 2011 ISPA proceedings and Journal of Convergence 2(1), 39-46
evidence_note: QFD chosen as method; 16 requirements identified after literature scan/focused-group discussion. Paper frames output as conceptual mapping and does not report an attack/control effectiveness experiment or quantitative consumer-trust validation.

title: General Privacy-Preserving Verifiable Incentive Mechanism for Crowdsourcing Markets
review_status: sample dispositioned; official arXiv record marks paper withdrawn due to crucial sign error in Equation 1 and Figure 1; not counted as full-text audit or valid positive evidence
venue_year_verified: arXiv v3 dated 2014-07-22; withdrawn by author
evidence_note: Do not rely on the former abstract's performance-parity claim; the author states the manuscript contains a crucial sign error in Eq. 1 and Fig. 1.

title: A privacy-preserving system for data ownership using blockchain and distributed databases
review_status: full-text audit complete after retry; architecture/prototype described, but no quantified privacy attack, formal proof, scalability measurement, or field evaluation reported
sections_checked: §II proposed ownership, trust, and data-separation assumptions
§III architecture: decentralized plaintext user-data store, identity databases, blockchain/SSI
venue_year_verified: arXiv v1 dated 2018-10-27; no venue publication verified
evidence_note: Full v1 PDF (8 pages) retrieved and extracted. Prototype stack is BigchainDB, MongoDB, private Ethereum node, and uPort. User-data records are stored in plaintext but described as de-identified; access is mediated through role-based APIs and identity fields are held separately. The paper discusses student/medical use cases but reports no quantified re-identification attack, formal privacy proof, performance/scaling benchmark, or field evaluation. This is an architecture proposal/prototype, not measured evidence of protection at scale.

title: Demystifying Swarm Learning: A New Paradigm of Blockchain-based Decentralized Federated Learning
review_status: full-text audit complete; training utility, poisoned-node counterexample, resource/scale scope, and threat-to-validity section checked; no formal DP or update-leakage attack evaluated
evidence_note: Raw data stay local while model parameters are exchanged; no formal DP guarantee or update-leakage attack test. With half of one node's labels corrupted, Task A/B SL accuracy is near centralized learning, but IMDB Task C drops from centralized 0.8646 to 0.7955. Evaluation uses 3-4 learning nodes and one SN node; proprietary blockchain implementation limits internal inspection.

title: Tangent differential privacy
review_status: full-text audit complete; theory/assumptions and definition scope checked; no empirical attack-defense benchmark
venue_year_verified: arXiv v1 dated 2024-06-06; published in Journal of Machine Learning in 2025
evidence_note: Distribution-specific tangent privacy theory under stated regularity/optimization conditions. Its adjacency/sensitivity notion is not directly interchangeable with record-level global DP or local edge DP; no empirical benchmark in audited paper.

title: Bomfather: An eBPF-based Kernel-level Monitoring Framework for Accurate Identification of Unknown, Unused, and Dynamically Loaded Dependencies in Modern Software Supply Chains
review_status: full-text audit complete; classified as security/supply-chain retrieval false positive for privacy-specific synthesis
sections_checked: Go 1.21.0 case study and reported counts
venue_year_verified: arXiv v1 dated 2025-03-03; no venue publication verified
evidence_note: One containerized Go compiler build reports 185,184 file-access events, 10,032 source files, 26 shared libraries, and 979 assembly files. Provenance/SBOM instrumentation is not a privacy guarantee or demonstrated vulnerability-prevention outcome.

title: Practical and Accurate Local Edge Differentially Private Graph Algorithms
review_status: full-text audit complete; edge-adjacency privacy definition, algorithm guarantees, graph-dependent utility, and single-machine distributed simulation scope checked
sections_checked: LEDP threat/adjacency model and algorithm guarantees
venue_year_verified: arXiv v3 dated 2025-08-27; publication status not verified
evidence_note: Reports improved approximation on selected real-world graphs under local edge DP, with utility dependent on epsilon and graph structure. Distributed framework is simulated on one machine; not a multi-machine deployment. Formal edge-level guarantee is not comparable to raw-data locality or tangent DP without aligning definitions.

title: Gradient Disaggregation: Breaking Privacy in Federated Learning by Reconstructing the User Participant Matrix
review_status: citation follow-up abstract/metadata checked; independent counterexample identified; full text not counted as audited
evidence_note: Authors report an untrusted server can separate user updates from repeated sums using participation information from device analytics, then improve inference attacks, including settings with thousands of participants. Treat as a threat-model-specific counterexample to assuming aggregation/local raw-data storage is sufficient.

title: Active Membership Inference Attack under Local Differential Privacy in Federated Learning
review_status: citation follow-up full-text audit complete; active malicious-server threat model, LDP attack experiments, utility and limitations checked
sections_checked: §5 benchmark results on CelebA, ImageNet, CIFAR-10
evidence_note: Under the paper's active dishonest-server threat model and studied BitRand mechanism, reported membership attack success is at least 0.77 for epsilon >= 5 and approaches 0.99 for epsilon >= 9; very low epsilon damages model accuracy. OME experiments report about 90% attack success for CelebA/CIFAR-10. This is not a universal LDP refutation; threat, mechanism, target, and utility matter.
